newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: France-Duisenberg decision does not prejudge ECB.
newsitem.headline: France-Duisenberg decision does not prejudge ECB.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told an EU summit that a decision to make Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg head of the European Monetary Institute did not mean he would automatically head the post-EMU European Central Bank.
"The decision on the nomination does not prejudge the presidency of the European Central Bank," Chirac's spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told a news briefing.
Chirac had made this point in the summit talks today, she said. "We will be in a new phase and no doubt there will have to be a new team and new personalities."

The EMI is the forerunner of the ECB, which is due to run monetary policy after economic and monetary union (EMU) is launched in 1999. It had been widely assumed that the next EMI chief would automatically head the ECB.
In a muted reaction, a Dutch diplomat said the Netherlands had never assumed that Duisenberg, confirmed to head the EMI from July 1997, would automatically move from the EMI to head the ECB.
One EU source said that there could be several candidates for the post of ECB chief.

Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet has long been believed to be interested in heading the ECB, but it is unclear how much support he has with President Chirac. The two have sparred in the past over policy.
